reason: Verified by driving, not by specificity argument. Playwright chromium, forcedColors:'active', 1440x960, master.html?v=approach&state=owner-flight. Computed values as shipped: .b-rail background-color = rgba(255,255,255,0.16) (should be CanvasText), .b-todayRule = rgb(255,255,255) (should be Highlight = rgb(55,0,110)), the lead tick's background = rgb(255,255,255) and border-top-color = rgb(0,0,0) (should be Highlight in both). I then sampled the composited pixels out of the real screenshot through a canvas: the rail column at x=686 reads 255,255,255 and the today rule at its own y reads 255,255,255 - identical to the page ground on both sides. Nothing is painted. The cause is exactly as stated: build.mjs concatenates fonts.css, shell.css, b.css, so the whole @media (forced-colors: active) block lands at master.html:355-369 while the base paint lands at 491 (.b-todayRule), 536 (.b-rail), 601 (.b-tick) and 678 (lead tick), same specificity, later, and a media query adds none. Chromium does not rescue it either: it leaves the author's rgba(255,255,255,0.16) and rgb(255,255,255) in place. Under colorScheme dark the same failure inverts - rail rgba(0,0,0,0.16) and today rgb(0,0,0) on a black Canvas - so it is invisible in both forced palettes, not one. Confirmed causally: injecting the identical block at the end of the cascade and changing nothing inside it flips the rail to rgb(0,0,0)/CanvasText with a real black pixel at x=686 and the today rule to rgb(55,0,110)/Highlight with a real indigo-violet pixel. The one survivor is the lead tick's border-width:3px, because b.css's line-678 block sets background, border-color, width, height, left and top but never border-width - which is precisely why the third gate assertion (geometry) still passes while the two colour assertions pass on invisible pixels: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.16)' and 'rgb(255,255,255)' are both !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)', so interaction-check.mjs:2093 and :2095 are satisfied by white on white. So this is not a restatement of anything the gates prove - it is a demonstration that two gate assertions are unfalsifiable as written. A high-contrast reader gets rows with no spine behind them and no statement of today on the rail. Real, specific, and a genuine defect at the 9.5 bar.
sharpenedFix: Move the @media (forced-colors: active) block from shell.css to the foot of b.css, after every rule it overrides - contents otherwise unchanged. Two additions the finding as written would miss, both measured. (1) In the 'record' room the fix still fails: [data-accent="structure"] .b-rail { background: var(--accent); opacity: 0.5 } at master.html:958 is specificity (0,2,0) and beats the block's .b-rail (0,1,0) no matter how late it sits - driven at v=record with the block moved last, the rail still computes rgb(255,255,255) at opacity 0.5. Add [data-accent="structure"] .b-rail { background: CanvasText; opacity: 1; } inside the block. (2) The .b-item[data-anchor="true"]::before ring computes border-top-width 0px even when the block applies, because the base rule declares no border-style; add border-style: solid alongside the border-width: 3px so the geometry survives there too. Then tighten interaction-check.mjs:2093 and :2095 from 'not transparent' to a real comparison against the ground: composite the element's background over the page background and assert the result differs from the page background (or simply assert the value equals the expected system colour - getComputedStyle returns CanvasText and Highlight as resolved rgb, so an equality check against the probed system-colour values is exact). Add the same check for the lead tick's border-top-color so 'the only filled mark' is proven by colour as well as by width, and run one assertion under colorScheme:'dark' so the inverted forced palette is covered.
